title: The Splendours Of South India
description:
Composed of the five states of Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Pondicherry  and Telangana, South India is a glistening paradise of World Heritage Sites, ancient history and pearlescent coastlines – a real feast for the senses. 

Our exclusive two-week stay will see you venture to a range of the region’s must-sees – from picture-perfect Pondicherry to mesmerizing Mysore, soaking up natural wonders and cultural gems during jam-packed sightseeing tours and thrilling excursions (including a bullock cart ride, cooking demonstration and jeep safari).  

Spend the first half of your getaway in Bangalore, Mysore, Kabini and Coonoor – each one wildly different and unique. 

Mysore is an eclectic hub and home to the opulent Mysore Palace and centuries-old, spice-scented Devaraja Market. Visit the Jayachamarajendra Art Gallery, Chamundeshwari Temple and feast your eyes upon the beauty of Brindavan Gardens. 

Then, spend a night at a critter-filled jungle resort in Kabini. Go on a safari through this impressive sanctuary spanning a whopping 55 acres before proceeding to the emerald-hued hill station of Coonoor in the state of Tamil Nadu – known for its bright green undulating landscapes and tea plantations (which you’ll have ample time to explore). 

For the second part of your trip, you’ll be whisked off to Madurai, Kumbakonam and Pondicherry. Your time in Madurai (an ancient city on the Vaigai River) will be spent visiting the Gandhi Museum and marveling at the techni coloured, awe-inspiring Meenakshi Amman Temple – a real treat to behold. 

And then in Kumbakonam, enjoy a rip-roaring bullock ride before making your way to Pondicherry (or Puducherry), a striking French colonial settlement. Meander along the seaside promenade, fringed by the Bay of Bengal, and pass by the Gandhi Memorial statue standing proud at four metres high. 

Lastly, you’ll spend three nights at a beach resort in Mamallapuram – a beautiful slice of paradise sitting between the Bay of Bengal and the Great Salt Lake. 

Known for its temples and monuments dating back to the Pallava dynasty, Mamallapuram is a great place for sightseeing – but also equally great for relaxing and unwinding. Resting your head at a luxurious 4* beach resort, you’re free to laze about by the pool or frolic about in the ocean for hours upon hours.

All applicable taxes
highlights: Revel in the sights and delights of the city of Mysore - with visits to Mysore Palace, Jayachamarajendra Art Gallery,Chamundi Hill & Rail museum  and the delightful Brindavan Gardens.

Visit the 55-acre Kabini Wildlife Sanctuary and stay in the jungle resort for a night – keeping your eyes peeled for long-tailed critters and sharp-toothed beasts such as leopards and panthers…you can add Elephants& Tigers
Visit the verdant hill station of Coonoor – brimming with tea plantations, sprawling gardens and vantage points with views of the spellbinding Catherine Falls
Take a sightseeing tour of picture-perfect Pondicherry, with visits to its thronging seaside promenade, the Grand Bazar, Pondicherry Museum and French War Memorial
Soak up South India’s stunning landscapes during a UNESCO mountain train ride from Coonoor to Ooty
Relax and unwind in the tropical paradise of Mamallapuram – you’ll be staying at a luxurious 4* beach resort, meaning there’s ample time for rest and relaxation.

itinerary.title: ARRIVAL IN BANGALORE
itinerary.description:
Welcome to the tech hub of Bangalore! Upon arrival at the airport, make your way to your respective hotel to check in and relax after your flight.

You’re free to spend today catching up on some shut-eye, unwinding in your hotel or heading out on an evening walk to buzzing areas such as MG Road, Cantonment area, Brigade Road, St Mark’s Road or UB City – a great place for shopping and one of Bangalore’s biggest commercial centres. 

Make your way back to the hotel for an overnight stay. 

OVERNIGHT IN BANGALORE

itinerary.title: BANGALORE TO MYSORE
itinerary.description:
After breakfast, check out at 10.30am and proceed to Mysore – a distance of 144km which takes 3.5 hours. 

En route, visit Srirangapatna Fort – an important historical site in Karnataka and boasting Indo-Islamic style architecture dating back to the 15th century. This fort owes its strength to the double walls and four majestic gates. Within it, you’ll find Sri Ranganathaswamy Temple, dedicated to Lord Vishnu and characterised by magnificent Vijayanagar and Hoysala style architecture. 

After visiting the fort and temple, make your way to St Philomena’s Cathedral in Mysore – one of India’s largest churches and the second largest in all of Asia. Tourists swarm to see its exceptionally beautiful Neo-Gothic and Victorian style architecture.

DINNER & OVERNIGHT IN MYSORE

itinerary.title: MYSORE SIGHTSEEING
itinerary.description:
After a hearty hotel breakfast, venture out into the splendid city of Mysore for a sightseeing tour commencing at around 10 00 am. First, visit the famous Mysore Palace, characterised by Indo-Saracenic architecture and one of the most beautiful palaces in the world. Built in 1912, it attracts visitors from far-flung corners of the globe.

Next, head to Jayachamarajendra Art Gallery and feast your eyes on Japanese furniture, paintings, woodcarvings, musical instruments and other artefacts spanning decades. 

Today you will also take a tour of the Mysore Railway Museum, home to vintage locomotives and established in 1979. Then, continue to Chamundi Hill for a spellbinding view of the city from 1000 metres up. If you have the energy, climb the 1008 steps up to the sacred Chamundeshwari Temple and Bull Statue. 

Finally, visit Brindavan Gardens – home to unique species of flora and fauna and terrace gardens with colourful fountains.

DINNER & OVERNIGHT IN MYSORE

itinerary.title: MYSORE TO KABINI
itinerary.description:
After breakfast, check out around 9am and head to Kabini – 96km away and a 2-hour journey. 

Upon arrival in Kabini, check in and relax before heading out to the famous Kabini Wildlife Sanctuary. This sprawling sanctuary covering 55 acres is home to dense forests, steep valleys, peaceful lakes and wild streams. 

Here, keep your eyes peeled for rare and exotic flora and fauna, including leopards, panthers, sambhars, spotted deer, chital and more than 250 species of birds. Enjoy an exciting boat or Jeep ride through the picturesque sanctuary during your stay too (subject to weather conditions).

DINNER & OVERNIGHT IN KABINI

itinerary.title: KABINI TO COONOOR VIA OOTY
itinerary.description:
Hunker down over a delicious breakfast before checkout. Depart for Coonoor at around 10:30 am – a journey totaling approximately 5 hours and covering a distance of 142 km. Coonoor is well known for its beautiful tea estates, peppering the surrounding Nilgiri Hills.

En route, take a lunch break at Ooty, after Lunch visit the Botanical Garden in Ooty and Proceed to Coonoor, check in at the hotel and spend the rest of the day relaxing.

DINNER & OVERNIGHT IN COONOOR

itinerary.title: COONOOR TO OOTY By TRAIN AND BACK to COONOOR (BY CAR)
itinerary.description:
Kick-start today with an early, nutritious breakfast before heading to Sim’s Park, one of Coonoor’s most popular attractions. This sprawling park/botanical garden is brimming with a wide range of vegetation and 150-year-old trees. 

Later Visit the Tea factory & Tea Garden. At Tea Factory you will learn about the origins of tea in the world and India.  You can witness the entire process of tea making right from plucking of tea leaves to the final product. Tea Garden comprises of tea plantation spread across vast area of land. You can understand the whole process of tea gardening which taking a tour through it.

Take lunch break at around 1 pm and later take a scenic train ride from Coonoor to Ooty. Built in 1908 by the British, it travels through undulating mountain landscapes, eerie tunnels and picture-perfect scenes. 

Once you arrive at Ooty railway station at 17:15 pm, driver will pick you from Ooty railway station and transfer you to the hotel in Coonoor at 18:15 pm.

DINNER & OVERNIGHT IN COONOOR

itinerary.title: COONOOR TO MADURAI
itinerary.description:
After breakfast, check out of the hotel around 10:30  and head to Madurai, your next destination. This 6-hour drive is very scenic. Upon arrival in Madurai, check in to your hotel and relax for the rest of the day.

Madurai is one of the oldest cities of India located in Tamil Nadu. It is also considered to be the cultural capital of the state. The 2,500 plus years old city, is known for its rich cultural heritage and strong mythological history. The city not only has a glorious past but also lively and busy present. 

The magnificent temples here flaunt the architectural brilliance of the artisans, culture and architectural marvels speak of the grandeur of this place. Most of these temples and monuments are constructed by Nayaka rulers during their reign    

The kingdom of Madurai passed hands between the Pandyas,  Kalabhra dynasty, Cholas, Delhi Sultanate, Vijayanagara empire, Nayaks and finally by Britishers before independence. 

OVERNIGHT IN MADURAI

itinerary.title: SIGHTSEEING IN MADURAI
itinerary.description:
Kick off your day with a hearty breakfast before proceeding to the culturally abundant city of Madurai – starting with the very famous Thirumalai Nayakar Palace. Built in the year 1635 by the King Thirumalai Nayak, the palace is a masterpiece for royal stay. It features an artistic blend of Dravidian and Islamic styles of architecture. Later head to St. Mary's Cathedral Church which over is over 150 years old. The church is known for its architectural brilliance and religious significance.

Around 12.30 pm, take lunch break and then visit the Gandhi Museum. It is home to writing material and other objects relating to Gandhi’s life. After delving deep into Gandhi’s history at the museum, make your way to Meenakshi Amman Temple, one of India’s oldest and most important Hindu temples. Dedicated to the Goddess Parvati and Lord Shiva, thousands of devotees visit the temple on a daily basis. 

OVERNIGHT IN MADURAI

itinerary.title: MADURAI TO KUMBAKONAM
itinerary.description:
After breakfast, check out and proceed to Kumbakonam – 219km away and a 4-hour drive. En route, stop off at Thanjavur and its sensational palace – home to Thanjavur paintings and statues from the Chola, Pallava, Pandiya and Nayaka periods. Thanjavur is also home to another UNESCO World Heritage Site, the Brihadisvara Temple – boasting unparalleled architecture and established by the Chola rulers in the 16th century.

Visit Thanjore Grand Maratha Palace and later visit Brihadisvara Temple in Thanjore. Around 1pm, take lunch break and then check in at Kumbakonam Heritage Resort. In the evening, enjoy a Bullock Cart ride at Kumabakonam subject to weather conditions.

OVERNIGHT IN KUMBAKONAM

itinerary.title: KUMBAKONAM TO PONDICHERRY
itinerary.description:
Following a hearty breakfast, Check out at 10:30 Hours  make your way to Airavatesvara temple, also known as Darasuram Temple. This World Heritage Site was built back in the 12th century and is dedicated to Lord Shiva.

Afternoon  head in the direction of Pondicherry – a total distance of 131 km and likely to take around 3 hours 10 minutes. Once you arrive in Pondicherry, check in to your hotel and spend the rest of the day unwinding. You’ll also have the chance to watch a cooking demonstration and learn a thing or two about South Indian cuisine.

OVERNIGHT IN PONDICHERRY

itinerary.title: SIGHTSEEING IN PONDICHERRY
itinerary.description:
Pondicherry is full of French colonial architecture – the French have had the greatest influence by far out of all the city’s visitors over the years. Pondicherry is also a buzzing cosmopolitan hub full to the brim with wonderful sights and delights such as the Sri Aurobindo Ashram premises, the Grand Bazar, Pondicherry Museum, the French War Memorial, the Aayi Mandapam Park Monument, the Promenade and Pondicherry Beach.

Kick start your tour with a visit to the Auroville (Matrimandir) and the Aurobindo Ashram. Matrimandir is spiritually significant for those who practice Integral Yoga, while Sri Aurobindo Ashram houses the Samadhi of Sri Aurobindo. Later visit Vinayaka Ganesh Temple. Also known as Arulmigu Manakula Vinayagar Devasthanam, this ancient temple was constructed over 500 years ago and it still stands in all its magnificent glory.

Later take a lunch Break at White Town, a popular shopping market,. Later on, proceed to the French War Memorial and pay respect to the brave soldiers who sacrificed their lives during WWI. Then, visit Our Lady of Angels Church and marvel at the rare oil painting of Our Lady of the Assumption and the fabulous Greek/Roman architecture.

Your next stop will be the Basilica of the Sacred Heart of Jesus – a church known for its opulent, elegant exteriors and neo-Gothic architecture. Founded in 1908, it is Pondicherry’s first basilica. After, make your way to the Seaside Promenade Beach and relax on this 1.5km stretch of glorious sand – home to iconic landmarks such as the Old Lighthouse, French War Memorial and Town Hall. Marvel at the mighty Mahatma Gandhi statue here, surrounded by eight granite pillars.

Later visit the Grand Bazar.

DINNER & OVERNIGHT IN PONDICHERRY

itinerary.title: DEPART FROM PONDICHERRY TO MAMMALLAPURAM
itinerary.description:
After breakfast, check out at 11 am and proceed to the last Destination Mammallapuram. Known affectionately as “The Temple City,” Mamallapuram is extraordinary to say the least – a glistening haven of UNESCO World Heritage Sites, surf spots and backpacker hangouts. Here, you can find some of India’s most popular beaches and luxurious resorts. It was also an important artistic, architectural and cultural hub between the 3rd and 7th century CE. 

On arrival, visit the Mammallapuram Shore Temples, Pancha Rathas, Ganesha Rathas & Sculpture Museum. Later, check in at your high-end beach resort.

DINNER & OVERNIGHT IN MAMALLAPURAM

itinerary.title: AT LEISURE IN MAMALLAPURAM
itinerary.description:
You’re free to spend today however you please, making the most of your beach resort facilities.

DINNER & OVERNIGHT IN MAMALLAPURAM

itinerary.title: AT LEISURE IN MAMALLAPURAM
itinerary.description:
Spend today relaxing by the pool or lapping up the scenic beach views from your resort. Alternatively, head out to explore the surrounding areas and sample some of the region’s delightful cuisine. 

DINNER & OVERNIGHT IN MAMALLAPURAM

itinerary.title: MAMALLAPURAM TO CHENNAI AIRPORT (45KM)
itinerary.description:
Today, after breakfast and check-out, head off shopping and sightseeing in Pondicherry before your flight from Chennai Airport. We hope you’ve had a wonderful holiday! 

END OF TOUR

title: Sri Lanka Heritage Tea Trail Jungles and Beaches
description:
Does spending ten days wandering around World Heritage Sites, visiting exquisite tea plantations and exploring an island once described by Marco Polo as “the finest island of its size in the world” sound like it would float your boat? Well, look no further.

Swap the gloomy, grey clouds of Britain for the glistening sun of Sri Lanka, an exotic island found at the tip of India, whose breathtaking beauty will have you begging for more by the end. Experience not only spectacular safaris and pristine beaches, but also a fascinating culture of honest, hard-working people whose love for their island runs deeper than you could possibly imagine. 

Whether your idea of a perfect holiday is to be firmly planted on a sunbed sipping Daiquiris until nightfall, or perhaps tearing up the wilderness while trying your hand at some adventure sports, exotic Sri Lanka has something for every traveler. 

Trekking, hiking and supervised dives under the deep, blue surf are on offer for any thrill-seekers out there, and an Ayuryedic wellness holiday may well be overdue for some of you who are looking to unwind from the hustle and bustle of back home. Even business trips don’t have to be all work and no play when visiting Sri Lanka. Our package not only includes excursions, hotels, transfers and dances, but also heritage train rides, bullock cart rides, cooking classes and massages. 

Lonely Planet describes Sri Lanka as “endless beaches, timeless ruins, welcoming people, rolling surf, fun trains and famous tea.” Why don’t you see if they’re right?

itinerary.title: ARRIVAL SIGIRIYA
itinerary.description:
Arrive in Sri Lanka,  Bandaranayke International Airport. There you will meet one of our representative and will be transfered to Sigiriya. 

COMPLIMENTARY MEAL ON ARRIVAL & OVERNIGHT IN SIGIRIYA

itinerary.title: SIGIRIYA / ROCK / VILLAGE HOUSE / SIGIRIYA
itinerary.description:
After breakfast leave for Rock Fortress which is is one of the most valuable historical monuments of Sri Lanka. Referred by locals as the Eighth Wonder of the World this ancient palace and fortress complex has significant archaeological importance and attracts thousands of tourists every year. It is probably the most visited tourist destination of Sri Lanka. Sigiriya rock plateau, formed from magma of an extinct volcano, is 200 meters higher than the surrounding jungles.

Later do you want to try something traditional and completely different? A delightful evening bullock cart ride is just the ticket, which will take you to some of the nicest places on the island. It’s pretty unconventional and definitely an adventure. Riding in the shade of the forests, you will see the country’s historic sites and some of the lovely scenery as well. What makes this ride exceptional is that you will visit a Sri Lankan village and enjoy a cookery demonstration and home-cooked meal from the local women and then top it off with a canoe ride across a beautiful lake! This tour will make your holiday that much more unforgettable! 

DINNER & OVERNIGHT IN SIGIRIYA

itinerary.title: SIGIRIYA / DAMBULLA / MINNERIYA / SIGIRIYA
itinerary.description:
After breakfast proceed to visit the Dambulla Rock Temple. Dambulla is a popular destination in the cultural triangle of Sri Lanka. With a history that dates back to the 1st century, Dambulla has historic statues and paintings in its caves that has made it a popular destination for archeological studies. This temple was built by King Walagambahu during the 1st Century B.C. Dambulla is a UNESCO world heritage site. There are more than 80 documented caves in the surrounding and the paintings are done on the ceiling. There are a total of 153 Buddha statues 3 statues of Sri Lankan kings and 4 statues of god and goddess.

Thereafter proceed on a jeep safari to visit the Minneriya National Park. The park is famous for being the best place in Sri Lanka to get close to free-ranging elephants. Bordering the Minneriya tank and the Giritale tank, the 7,529 hectare park attracts hundreds of elephants during the dry season, as surrounding water source dries up. Watching them travel in herds of 10 to 20, it is impossible not to be impressed with the sheer bulk of a fully grown adult, but equally spectacular is seeing how they interact. There is also a host of water birds, both large and small, so keep your eyes open for delicately hued storks, slender and elegant grey herons, and great white pelicans.

DINNER & OVERNIGHT IN SIGIRIYA

itinerary.title: SIGIRIYA / MATALE/ KANDY
itinerary.description:
After breakfast you will leave for Kandy. Just 25 km from the hill capital of Kandy, the Matale spice gardens are among the best on the island where you will be introduced to different types of spices. Here you will also be shown how some of these spices are grown and processed. Visitors may buy spices, traditional remedies and cosmetics, taste a herbal brew and in some venues.

In Matale, you will also enjoy the full flavors of Sri Lankan spices over lunch or an Ayurveda massage based on natural products from the garden.

Evening at leisure.

DINNER & OVERNIGHT IN KANDY

itinerary.title: KANDY (SIGHTSEEING)
itinerary.description:
After breakfast, proceed on a sightseeing tour of Kandy - which was the last capital of the Sri Lankan kings, and is a World Heritage Site. The name Kandy conjures visions of splendor and magnificence. Many of the legends, traditions and folklore are still lovingly kept alive. Drive around the Kandy Lake built by the last Sinhala King Sri Wickrama Rajasinghe in 1798. Visit the Kandy town and Bazaar, the arts & crafts centre and a gem museum and a lapidary.  

In the evening visit the Temple of the Tooth Relic and thereafter witness a cultural show featuring traditional Sri Lankan dancing.

DINNER & OVERNIGHT IN KANDY

itinerary.title: KANDY TO NUWARA ELIYA ( TRAIN RIDE )
itinerary.description:
After breakfast, proceed to the Kandy Train Station to board the Train leaving for Nanu Oya – It is an unforgettable train ride to Nuwara Eliya. Sit back in the comfort where from you can catch jaw-dropping views as the train powers up through the tea plantations, into the clouds and then weaves in and out of the many mountain tunnels. The railway in Sri Lanka was first introduced by the British Colonial government in 1864, to transport tea from places like Nuwara Eliya to the capital, Colombo.

Nuwara Eliya which is at an elevation of 1890 meters above the sea level is the highest city in Sri Lanka and it lies beneath the tallest peak of the island. Nuwara Eliya (City of Lights) is a resort city blessed with salubrious climate, breathtaking views of valleys, meadows, mountains and greenery. Nuwara Eliya, also known as ‘Little’ England’, was the favorite hill station of the British who tried to create the resort into a typical English Village.  

DINNER & OVERNIGHT IN NUWARA ELIYA

itinerary.title: NUWARA ELIYA – KOGGALA
itinerary.description:
After breakfast, travel through the twisting roads. It is then onto the beautiful village of Kitulgala; with forest-covered hills plunging down to the wild waters of the Kelani Ganga, astounding waterfalls and towering trees, the scenery is particularly dramatic. Kitulgala’s original claim to fame is as the location for David Lean’s 1957 film “Bridge on the River Kwai”. Nowadays, Kitulgala is best known as the site of Sri Lanka’s best white water rafting with grade two and grade three rapids some 5km upriver from the village.

After lunch we then head for the paradise beaches of Koggala. En route we visit the town’s Turtle Hatchery. Koggala is one of Sri Lanka’s most import ant breeding spots for the endangered Sea Turtles.

The sandy beaches serve as sanctuary for several types of marine turtles including Loggerheads and the Leatherback Turtle. The small turtle hatchery first opened in 1996, in an effort to promote responsible tourism and conservation. The hatchery buys turtle eggs off fishermen, in an attempt to discourage them from poaching and selling the eggs.

You will be educated on the importance of protecting turtle life, via the hatchery’s facilities that care for new born turtles until they are ready to be released back into the ocean, an experience that you may even have the opportunity to do yourself first-hand! Continue to hotel.

DINNER & OVERNIGHT IN KOGGALA

itinerary.title: KOGGALA
itinerary.description:
A relatively unknown when it comes to beach escapes, Koggala is authentic, captivating and entirely without guile and location-wise it doesn’t get much better than this. The small coastal town stretches across the south coast of Sri Lanka and has one of the island nation’s longest beaches, where you can explore the reef straight from the beach.

A stay here takes your Sri Lanka adventure to an altogether different level, bringing together the exceptional and beautiful in one special paradise.

After breakfast, enjoy a relaxing day at leisure. Your beautiful hotel is set beside the sublime sands and coconut palms of Koggala Beach.Take a walk along the coast to look out for turtles wading in the shallows.

Retire to the serenity of the spa for a soothing treatment or lounge beside the outdoor pool and be pampered. Nearby to the historic city of Galle, its famous fort is a site you will not once to miss and between November and April feel free to join a whale watching excursion at nearby Mirissa.

DINNER & OVERNIGHT IN KOGGALA

itinerary.title: KOGGALA
itinerary.description:
End your holiday in this very beautiful and relaxing part of Sri Lanka by reclining on the golden sandy beaches or sipping cocktails overlooking the sunset.

If you keep your eyes open you might even see the Green Flash! A sudden short pinprick of green that happens as the sun sinks towards the horizon.

DINNER & OVERNIGHT IN KOGGALA

itinerary.title: KOGGALA – COLOMBO--UK
itinerary.description:

title: Singles Holiday to Sri Lanka with meals, excursions and flights
description:
Sri Lanka is known for its stunning beaches, dense rain forests, wide selection of fascinating wildlife and wonderful Buddhist ruins. You can meet gentle elephants and watch whales frolic in the ocean, as well as exploring some of the ancient ruins. Due to its history as a maritime hub, the cuisine in the area is a rich fusion of many cultural influences, taking the best bits from other destinations and combining them in an impression and memorable array of delicious dishes.

A rich cultural heritage and some of the best ayurvedic spas in the world are all reasons that Sri Lanka makes an enchanting destination for your singles holiday experience. The golden beaches of the country had been praised for their picture postcard views since eternity. The dusk and dawn and many human activities connected to these times of the day creates a vibrant picture along the coasts of Sri Lanka. Whether your tastes are with cultural exploration, flavorful cuisine or water sports such as diving and swimming, you’ll find everything you need on a singles holiday to Sri Lanka.

itinerary.title: ARRIVAL / TRANSFER / COLOMBO
itinerary.description:
Arrive in Sri Lanka, Bandaranayke International Airport. There you will meet one of our representative and will be transfered to Colombo.

If time permits enjoy the Colombo Sightseeing Tour. The city skyline has dramatically changed during the last decade, trendy malls and cafes sit alongside old colonial architectural monuments and local eateries. The city tour will take you pass the Colombo harbor to the area known as the Fort, the islands administrative and main banking quarter adjoining the famous Dutch Hospital and the esplanade known as the Galle Face. The colorful religious edifices that adorn the different zones in the city reflect the countries multi-ethnic, religious and cultural diversity. The Cinnamon Gardens, the ‘chic’ residential section of Colombo with its numerous villas and mansions blends well with the recently restored Race- Course and Victoria Park. The Gangaramaya Temple with its collection of oriental antiquities and Buddhist manuscripts offers visitors a completely different turn-around from the rich and grand archaeological monuments of Sri Lanka.

Please Note: **If flight will arrive after 1330 Hrs, Colombo Sightseeing tour will be not included**

DINNER & OVERNIGHT IN COLOMBO

itinerary.title: COLOMBO / DAMBULLA
itinerary.description:
Following an early breakfast at hotel you will leave for Dambulla. En route visit the Dambulla Rock Temple - Climb up to the temple, which was donated by king Walagambahu in the 1st century BC to Buddhist monks, Dambulla is a World Heritage site and is the most impressive of Sri Lanka’s cave temples. The complex of five caves with over 2000 sq. meters of painted walls and the ceiling is the largest area of paintings found in the world. These caves contain over 150 images of the Buddha of which the largest is the colossal figure of the Buddha carved out of rock spanning 14 meters. 

Want to try something traditional and completely different? A delightful evening bullock cart ride is just the ticket, which will take you to some of the nicest places on the island. It’s pretty unconventional and definitely an adventure. Riding in the shade of the forests, you will see the country’s historic sites and some of the lovely scenery as well. What makes this ride exceptional is that you will visit a Sri Lankan village and enjoy a cookery demonstration and home-cooked meal from the local women and then top it off with a canoe ride across a beautiful lake! This tour will make your holiday that much more unforgettable!

DINNER & OVERNIGHT IN DAMBULLA

itinerary.title: DAMBULLA / SIGIRIYA /  MINNERIYA / DAMBULLA
itinerary.description:
Enjoy a delicious and healthy breakfast. Later, proceed on a jeep safari to visit the Minneriya National Park. The park is famous for being the best place in Sri Lanka to get close to free-ranging elephants. Bordering the Minneriya tank and the Giritale tank, the 7,529 hectare park attracts hundreds of elephants during the dry season, as surrounding water source dries up. Watching them travel in herds of 10 to 20, it is impossible not to be impressed with the sheer bulk of a fully grown adult, but equally spectacular is seeing how they interact. There is also a host of water birds, both large and small, so keep your eyes open for delicately hued storks, slender and elegant grey herons, and great white pelicans.

DINNER & OVERNIGHT IN DAMBULLA

itinerary.title: DAMBULLA / MATALE / KANDY
itinerary.description:
After breakfast you will leave for Kandy. Just 25 km from the hill capital of Kandy, the Matale spice gardens are among the best on the island. Here you will be introduced to different types of spices Sri Lanka is famous for and and will also be shown how some of these spices are grown and processed. Visitors may buy spices, traditional remedies and cosmetics, taste a herbal brew and in some venues.

In Matale, you will also enjoy the full flavors of Sri Lankan spices over lunch. Evening at leisure.

DINNER & OVERNIGHT IN KANDY

itinerary.title: KANDY
itinerary.description:
After breakfast, proceed on a sightseeing tour of Kandy - which was the last capital of the Sri Lankan kings, and is a World Heritage Site. The name Kandy conjures visions of splendor and magnificence. Many of the legends, traditions and folklore are still lovingly kept alive. Drive around the Kandy Lake built by the last Sinhala King Sri Wickrama Rajasinghe in 1798. Visit the Kandy town and Bazaar, the arts & crafts centre and a gem museum and a lapidary. 

In the evening visit the Temple of the Tooth Relic and thereafter witness a cultural show featuring traditional Sri Lankan dancing.

DINNER & OVERNIGHT IN KANDY

itinerary.title: KANDY/NUWARA ELIYA
itinerary.description:
After breakfast, proceed to the Kandy Train Station to board the Train leaving for Nanu Oya – It is an unforgettable train ride to Nuwara Eliya. Sit back in the comfort from where you can catch jaw-dropping views as the train powers up through the tea plantations, into the clouds and then weaves in and out of the many mountain tunnels. The railway in Sri Lanka was first introduced by the British Colonial government in 1864, to transport tea from places like Nuwara Eliya to the capital, Colombo.

Nuwara Eliya which is at an elevation of 1890 meters above the sea level is the highest city in Sri Lanka and it lies beneath the tallest peak of the island. Nuwara Eliya (City of Lights) is a resort city blessed with salubrious climate, breathtaking views of valleys, meadows, mountains and greenery. Nuwara Eliya, also known as ‘Little’ England’, was the favorite hill station of the British who tried to create the resort into a typical English Village.

title: An Ultimate Getaway to Sri Lanka & Maldives
description:
They say there is no other country in the world, like Sri Lanka. A smiling sun all year round, golden beaches, ancient cities, exciting safaris, colorful culture, adventure sport and lovely people… where else can you get all these in one place? Your last four nights will be spent in an unforgettable manner, rubbing shoulders with sea turtles beneath the aquamarine Indian Ocean in the heart of the Maldives.

During your five nights’ stay in Sri Lanka, it is safe to say you’ll be spoilt for choice. The island offers a wide range of activities for every type of traveler, whether you are somebody who likes to keep cool as a cucumber poolside with a mojito in hand, or perhaps a secret thrill-seeker at heart whose idea of a perfect holiday involves a bit of rock climbing or a splash of water sports. Our package not only includes excursions, hotels, transfers and dances, but also heritage train rides, bullock cart rides, cooking classes and massages. 

The adventure of a lifetime begins in Sri Lanka’s Capital Colombo, a port city, with a rich colonial heritage, religions and cultures. Then you will visit Sigiriya, a historical ancient city sprinkled with royal palaces, Buddhist frescoes and World Heritage Sites. Spend 2 nights’ in Kandy, one of the cultural hubs of the island which also houses the famous Temple of the Tooth, the Matale Spice Gardens as well as Kandy Lake which you will drive around in the evening. No need to fret though, after such a jam-packed day, you’ll be able to rest your weary feet at the Topaz Hotel Kandy Hotel.

Next, prepare to be whisked off on a memorable train ride in Sri Lanka’s most popular hill station, Nuwara Eliya through tea plantations, twisting and turning through the mountain tunnels high up in the fluffy clouds. Catch a flight from Colombo to Malé where you’ll be transferred to your Certificate of Excellence Hotel in true A-list style, via speedboat. 

There is no better place to relax and wind down than in one of the most stunning corners of the world, the Maldives.  A haven for tropical weather and exotic marine life, Adaaran Select Hudhuranfashi is one of the larger islands which will be your own personal slice of paradise for the next four nights. Not only is it a place providing ultimate rest and relaxation, but it is also one of the best surfing resorts in the Maldives.

On arrival in Nuwara Eliya proceed on a sightseeing tour, the city is tucked away within the hill country of the Central Province. The town is renowned for its lush tea plantations, waterfalls, red-roofed English country style houses, a golf course and a manmade lake. Nuwara Eliya is nicked named “Little England” because it was established by the British in the 1840s as a base for the colonists and still retains some distinctive English features, like the red post box and the Queen’s Cottage. title: 12 Days In Cambodia And Vietnam
description:
“Southeast Asia is a fulfilment of my fantasies of the way travel should be.”- Anthony Bourdain

Cambodia and Vietnam are breathtaking destinations of diverse delights. Travelers are gripped by the sights and sounds, bewitched by their geniality and divine cuisine, captivated by fast-moving cities like Ho Chi Minh, the Mecca in which Vietnam flourishes, and enlightened by  the palaces, cathedrals and the thousands of stalagmites of Sung Sot cave. Such a concoction of history, French colonial influences, and tales of past upheaval ensures a majestic holiday.

During our fantastic 12 day trip across Cambodia and Vietnam, undergo an exhilarating renovation of the senses. Venture into the jungle’s vines and creepers towards Angkor Wat, the 12th century temple and shrine of Khmer art and architecture, a Cambodian mascot with its sculpted towers of lotus blossom and stately surroundings worshipped by Buddhists monks.

Wander through the ancient capital of Khmer, empire to the exuberant cities of Siem Reap, Ho Chi Minh and Hanoi, before cruising in Agatha Christie style across Halong Bay, passing some of the 3,000 limestone islands. Add spice by devouring the Vietnamese cuisine of B?n Thành Market infused with a vast spectrum of enticing and evocative flavours, making taste buds explode. “I changed my whole palate as a lot of the dishes I used to love became boring to me.” - Anthony Bourdain.

itinerary.title: ARRIVAL SIEM REAP
itinerary.description:
You will be received with a warm welcome at Siem Reap International airport and transferred to the hotel.

The evening is free for you to relax at the hotel. In case you wish to explore the city, you can choose to visit Pub Street which
is famous for its quality yet economical restaurants and bars. Enjoy Khmer dinner on the day of arrival.

OVERNIGHT IN SIEM REAP

itinerary.title: ANGKOR TOUR
itinerary.description:
After a sumptuous breakfast at the hotel, you’ll enjoy a full-day tour of the Angkor complex.

You must not miss the antique capital of Angkor Thom. With sites like the South Gate with its huge statues depicting the churning of the ocean of milk; the Bayon Temple, unique for its 54 towers decorated with over 200 smiling faces of Avolokitesvara; the Phimeanakas; the Royal Enclosure; the Elephants Terrace and the Terrace of the Leper King; Angkor Thom has so much to offer.

The most famous of all the temples on the plain of Angkor is Angkor Wats. The temple complex covers 81 hectares and is comparable in size to the Imperial Palace in Beijing. Its distinctive five towers are emblazoned on the Cambodian flag and the 12th century masterpiece is considered by art historians to be the prime example of classical Khmer art and architecture.

Other sites that deserve a mention are: Prasat Kravan, also known as ‘The Royal Baths’, the site was once used for ritual bathing; Banteay Kdei, surrounded by 4 concentric walls; Neak Pean, a fountain built in the middle of a pool; Preah Khan temple, built by the King Jayavarman VII.

OVERNIGHT IN SIEM REAP

itinerary.title: SIEM REAP AT LEISURE OR OPTIONAL BOAT TRIP
itinerary.description:
After eating breakfast at the hotel, your day will be at leisure or you may head out to enjoy an optional boat ride on the Tonle Sap Lake.

This beautiful fresh-water lake is the largest in South-east Asia and flows into Tonle Sap River, joining the Mekong in Phnom Penh. Built on the lake, is a wondrous ‘floating village’ with floating schools, floating police station, et al. The ‘village’ moves from place to place following water levels and current.

OVERNIGHT IN SIEM REAP

itinerary.title: SIEM REAP - PHNOM PENH
itinerary.description:
After breakfast get ready for a coach journey from Siem Reap to Phnom Penh. On arrival, you will meet one of our representative and transferred to your hotel in Phnom Penh. Continue your journey in the Pearl of the Orient, Phnom Penh, visiting by yourself the dazzling white and gold complex of the Royal Palace and the Silver Pagoda. 

Feel free to visit the Genocide Museum or venture to the former Tuol Svay Prey High School, which the Khmer Rouge set up as prison in May 1976, to detain those accused of opposing the Pol Pot regime. Be prepared to be shaken by this moving reminder of the genocide that occurred during Cambodia’s Khmer Rouge regime.

OVERNIGHT IN PHNOM PENH

itinerary.title: PHNOM PENH - HO CHI MINH CITY
itinerary.description:
After breakfast at the hotel, you be transferred to Phnom Penh bus station for coach transfer to Ho Chi Minh City (still called Saigon by many locals). Upon arrival at Ho Chi Minh City, you are transferred to the hotel.

If there’s time, you must stroll around the downtown part of the bustling Ho Chi Minh City to explore the different local ways of life. Ho Chi Minh City, still called Saigon by many locals, is a centre of commerce, finance, culture and tourism in Vietnam. As opposed to its northern counterpart, this metropolis is filled with automobiles, numerous shopping areas and sidewalk cafes.

OVERNIGHT IN HO CHI MINH CITY

itinerary.title: HO CHI MINH CITY SIGHTS & CU CHI TUNNELS EXCURSION
itinerary.description:
The plan is to devote half of today exploring the captivating Ho Chi Minh City.

We pass by the now-demolished wartime American Embassy on our way to the Reunification Palace. This famous edifice was a former residence of the President of Southern Vietnam until end of April 1975.

We also visit some striking French colonial structures including the Notre Dame Cathedral and the Old Saigon Post Office. Post this, we head to the Jade Emperor Pagoda and the War Remnant Museum. We conclude our sightseeing session with a walk around the retail Ben Thanh Market where anything and everything is for sale!

In the afternoon, we travel about 30 km North-West of Ho Chi Minh City to Cu Chi town. 

Cu Chi tunnels were used as the base from which the Vietnamese mounted their operations of the Tet Offensive in 1968. The incredible underground network in Cu Chi stretched over 200 kilometres and became legendary during the American war.

The extensive tunnels have been specially constructed with living areas, weapon factories, filed hospitals, command centres, plus accommodation. We visit an exposition hall and a widened section of the tunnels to get a feel of the underground life. There are also possibilities to fire off rounds from an AK47 or MK16 at the nearby rifle range.

OVERNIGHT IN HO CHI MINH CITY

After breakfast our boat will continue to cruise in marvelous areas, where almost each islet has its own name, adopting its shape or reminiscent like Sail Island, Fisherman’s head rock, Butterfly rock or Turtle islet etc. Check out your room and have brunch on board while the cruise coming back the pier. title: 14 Nights Trip To Thailand Cambodia and Vietnam
description:

Experience the cultural richness and unique market scenes of Thailand with this comprehensive tour. Begin in Bangkok with visits to three significant temples: Wat Trimit, housing a 3-meter tall Buddha statue made of 5.5 tons of solid gold; Wat Pho, featuring Bangkok's largest reclining Buddha statue at 46 meters long and home to the birthplace of traditional Thai massage; and Wat Benchamabophit, the Marble Temple, built from white Italian marble and housing one of the country's most beautiful Buddha images.

 After exploring these spiritual sites, head to the Maeklong Railway Market, also known as Talad Rom Hup ("Umbrella Pulldown Market"), where you'll witness the unique sight of market stalls being pulled back to let trains pass through. Finally, visit the Damnoen Saduak Floating Market, reached by a short paddleboat ride, where vendors sell goods directly from their boats. Enjoy the vibrant atmosphere and sample local specialties like mango sticky rice. This tour offers a memorable glimpse into Thailand's Buddhist heritage and bustling market culture.

During this fantastic trip, undergo an exhilarating renovation of the senses. Venture into the jungle’s vines and creepers towards Angkor Wat, the 12th century temple and shrine of Khmer art and architecture, a Cambodian mascot with its sculpted towers of lotus blossom and stately surroundings worshiped by Buddhists monks.

Next up is Vietnam with are breathtaking destinations of diverse delights. Travelers are gripped by the sights and sounds, bewitched by their geniality and divine cuisine, captivated by fast-moving cities like Ho Chi Minh, the Mecca in which Vietnam flourishes, and enlightened by  the palaces, cathedrals and the thousands of stalagmites of Sung Sot cave.

Such a concoction of history, French colonial influences, and tales of past upheaval ensures a majestic holiday. This trip also includes an Overnight Cruise in the Halong bay, a UNESCO world heritage Site. Full Board and with a lot of Sights & activities along the way.

OVERNIGHT IN BANGKOK

itinerary.title: Bangkok Temples Half Day Tour
itinerary.description:
This half-day tour in Bangkok offers a chance to visit three of the city's most significant temples, each renowned for their cultural value and Buddhist sacredness. The first stop is Wat Trimit, the Temple of the Golden Buddha, a modern temple built to house a 3-meter tall Buddha statue crafted from 5.5 tons of solid gold. This gleaming Sukhothai style statue was accidentally discovered after a painted and decorated statue was dropped during relocation, revealing the beautiful solid gold Buddha inside. As you pass through Chinatown, you'll visit Wat Pho, the Temple of the Reclining Buddha. This temple, one of Bangkok's oldest, features the city's largest Buddha statue, measuring 46 meters in length and 15 meters in height, illustrating the Buddha's passing into nirvana. Wat Pho is also home to Thailand's largest collection of Buddha images, the country's first university, and is the birthplace of traditional Thai massage. The final stop is Wat Benchamabophit, the Marble Temple, built in the 19th century from white Italian marble from Carrara. This monastery houses one of the country's most beautiful Buddha images. This tour provides a glimpse into Thailand's rich Buddhist heritage and showcases some of Bangkok's most iconic and architecturally stunning temples.

OVERNIGHT IN BANGKOK

itinerary.title: Maeklong Railway Market and Damnoen Saduak Floating Market Tour
itinerary.description:
This tour takes you to two of Thailand's most unique and vibrant markets: the Maeklong Railway Market and the Damnoen Saduak Floating Market.

 The first stop is the Maeklong Railway Market, also known as Talad Rom Hup, or the “Umbrella Pulldown Market.” This market is one of the largest fresh seafood markets in Thailand and is situated right on the tracks of the Maeklong Railway. With your local guide, gain fascinating insights into the market's operations and the variety of products sold. Marvel at how the market stalls and awnings are pulled back from the tracks every time a train approaches, allowing the train to pass through.

 Next, you'll visit the Damnoen Saduak Floating Market, one of the most famous floating markets in Thailand. To reach the market, take a short ride in a paddleboat. Enjoy plenty of time to explore this colorful market, where friendly vendors sell their goods directly from boats. Take in the sights and sounds, and sample local specialties like mango sticky rice. Your guide will provide recommendations on what not to miss. The tour returns to Bangkok in time for the early afternoon.

OVERNIGHT IN BANGKOK

itinerary.title: ARRIVE SIEM REAP--DAY AT LEISURE
itinerary.description:
You will be received with a warm welcome at Siem Reap International airport and transferred to the hotel.

The evening is free for you to relax at the hotel. In case you wish to explore the
city, you can choose to visit Pub Street which is famous for its quality yet economical restaurants and bars. Enjoy Khmer dinner on the day of arrival.

OVERNIGHT IN SIEM REAP

itinerary.title: FULL DAY ANGKOR TOUR
itinerary.description:
After a sumptuous breakfast at the hotel, you’ll enjoy a full-day tour of the Angkor complex.

The most famous of all the temples on the plain of Angkor is Angkor Wats. The temple complex covers 81 hectares and is comparable in size to the Imperial Palace in Beijing.

Its distinctive five towers are emblazoned on the Cambodian flag and the 12th century masterpiece is considered by art historians to be the prime example of classical Khmer art and architecture.

You must not miss the antique capital of Angkor Thom. 

With sites like the South Gate with its huge statues depicting the churning of the ocean of milk; the Bayon Temple, unique for its 54 towers decorated with over 200 smiling faces of Avolokitesvara; the Phimeanakas; the Royal Enclosure; the Elephants Terrace and the Terrace of the Leper King; Angkor Thom has so much to offer.

Other sites that deserve a mention are: Prasat Kravan, also known as ‘The Royal Baths’, the site was once used for ritual bathing; Banteay Kdei, surrounded by 4 concentric walls; Neak Pean, a fountain built
in the middle of a pool; Preah Khan temple, built by the King Jayavarman VII.

OVERNIGHT IN SIEM REAP

itinerary.title: SIEM REAP - DAY AT LEISURE OR OPTIONAL BOAT TRIP
itinerary.description:
After enjoying breakfast at the hotel, your day will be at leisure or you may head out to enjoy an optional boat ride on the Tonle Sap Lake.

This beautiful fresh-water lake is the largest in South-east Asia and flows into Tonle Sap River, joining the Mekong in Phnom Penh. Built on the lake, is a wondrous ‘floating village’ with floating schools, floating police station, et al. The ‘village’ moves from place to place following water levels and current.

OVERNIGHT IN SIEM REAP

itinerary.title: SIEM REAP - PHNOM PENH
itinerary.description:
After breakfast get ready for a coach journey from Siem Reap to Phnom Penh. On arrival, you will meet one of our representative and transferred to your hotel in Phnom Penh.

Continue your journey in the Pearl of the Orient, Phnom Penh, visiting by yourself the dazzling white and gold complex of the Royal Palace and the Silver Pagoda.

Feel free to visit the Genocide Museum or venture to the former Tuol Svay Prey High School, which the Khmer Rouge set up as prison in May 1976, to detain those accused of opposing the Pol Pot regime.
Be prepared to be shaken by this moving reminder of the genocide that occurred during Cambodia’s Khmer Rouge regime.

OVERNIGHT IN PHNOM PENH

itinerary.title: PHNOM PENH - HO CHI MINH CITY
itinerary.description:
After breakfast at the hotel, you be transferred to Phnom Penh bus 
station for coach transfer to Ho Chi Minh City (still called Saigon by 
many locals). Upon arrival at Ho Chi Minh City, you are transferred to the hotel. If there’s time, you must stroll around the downtown part of the bustling Ho Chi Minh City to explore the different local ways of life. Ho Chi Minh City, still called Saigon by many locals, is a centre of commerce, finance, culture and tourism in Vietnam. As opposed to its northern counterpart, this metropolis is filled with automobiles, numerous shopping areas and sidewalk cafes.

OVERNIGHT IN HO CHI MINH CITY

itinerary.title: HO CHI MINH CITY SIGHTS & CU CHI TUNNELS EXCURSION
itinerary.description:
The plan is to devote half of today to exploring captivating Ho Chi Minh City. We pass by the now-demolished wartime American Embassy on our way to the Reunification Palace. This famous edifice
was a former residence of the President of Southern Vietnam until end of April 1975. We also visit some striking French colonial structures including the Notre Dame Cathedral and the Old Saigon Post Office.

Post this, we head to the Jade Emperor Pagoda and the War Remnant Museum. We conclude our sightseeing
session with a walk around the retail Ben Thanh Market where anything and everything is for sale!

 In the afternoon, we travel about 30 km North-West of Ho Chi Minh City to Cu Chi town.

Cu Chi tunnels were used as the base from which the Vietnamese mounted their operations of the Tet Offensive in 1968.

The incredible underground network in Cu Chi stretched over 200 kilometres and became legendary during the American war. 

The extensive tunnels have been specially constructed with living areas, weapon factories, filed hospitals, command centres, plus accommodation. We visit an exposition hall and a widened section of the tunnels to get a feel of the underground life.

There are also possibilities to fire off rounds from an AK47 or MK16 at the nearby rifle range.

OVERNIGHT IN HO CHI MINH CITY

itinerary.title: SAIGON - HANOI OR EXTEND TO DANANG IF OPTIONAL HOI AN EXTENSION IS CHOSEN
itinerary.description:
Step back in time as you fly from the buzzing, modern city of Ho Chi Minh to Hanoi. Upon arrival at Noi Bai international airport, you’ll be transferred to your hotel in Hanoi. Afternoon / Evening at leisure to
explore the evening sights on your own.

OVERNIGHT IN HANOI

itinerary.title: HANOI - HALONG PIER - LA REGINA ROYAL CRUISE
itinerary.description:
You will get picked up at the hotel lobby for a road journey to Halong by a shuttle bus.Upon arrival in Halong, check in the overnight cruise to discover the magnificent beauty of this “Descending-dragon” bay, created by thousands odd-shaped limestone rocks and karst grottoes. After a lunch on board, we can visit the Grottos, stop for swimming or kayaking, passing floating houses and approach islets to enjoy their beauty in close distance. Back to the cruise, enjoy cooking demonstration before having dinner. Evening attend activities on the boat or relax at your own leisure

OVERNIGHT ON CRUISE

itinerary.title: LA REGINA ROYAL CRUISE - HALONG PIER
itinerary.description:
The day starts early and has a lot of adventures to offer.
06:15: Tai Chi class on the Sun-Deck
07:00: Have light breakfast with Coffee, tea, and bakeries on board.
 You should wake up early to enjoy the dawn on the sea in the early morning. The Vietnamese call the "East Sea" by a point-oriented name "Eastern Sea", so you may guess how miraculous seeing the sunrise over the islets of the Bay. After breakfast our boat will continue to cruise in marvelous areas, where almost each islet has its own name, adopting its shape or reminiscent like Sail Island, Fisherman’s head rock, Butterfly rock or Turtle islet etc. Check out your room and have brunch on board while the cruise coming back the pier. Disembark from the cruise, transfer back to hotel in Hanoi.

OVERNIGHT IN HANOI

itinerary.title: HANOI
itinerary.description:
After breakfast at the hotel, you will enjoy a walking tour of the Ho Chi Minh complex, the Ho Chi Minh’s Mausoleum - the final resting place of Vietnamese great father; President Ho Chi Minh’s stilt house - where Ho lived on and off from 1958 to 1969.

The next place is One Pillar Pagoda, a group of structures consisting of a pagoda and a tower built in the middle of a square pond.

From there, leave for the Temple of Literature, the first college of Vietnam. 

While heading back to Hoan Kiem Lake, have a brief stopover at Ngoc Son Temple.

In the evening, experience the Water Puppet Show near the lake and later you can enjoy a relaxing 30 minutes spa session.

OVERNIGHT IN HANOI

itinerary.title: HANOI - DAY AT LEISURE
itinerary.description:
Have a leisurely breakfast at the hotel and later you may choose to take an optional Cyclo tour (at an additional cost) around the Old Quarter Streets.

OVERNIGHT IN HANOI

itinerary.title: HANOI - BACK TO UK OR TAKE OUR OPTIONAL HOI AN TRIP
itinerary.description:
After breakfast at the hotel, you can devote the entire day to shopping and buying souvenirs for friends.

As the hotel is located in central Hanoi, all the shopping areas are not too far. Then, according to your flight schedule, you shall be driven to the airport.

END THE TOUR

Le Petite Salil Sukhumvit 11, Bangkok

 Nestled down a small, quiet street off the Sukhumvit road, La Petite Salil Sukhumvit 11 awaits to welcome guests with its unique charm and character. World-class shopping malls, fine dining restaurants, night markets, and nightlife that are in the vicinity make this hotel’s location superb. Just a 5-minute walk to Nana BTS skytrain station, the hotel has a relaxed ambience, perfect for unplugging and recharging before the next day's adventures. Besides the dedicated guest rooms. the hotel also has facilities that a decent urban hotel has to offer –elevator, shuttle service from and to Nana BTS skytrain station, and free high speed Wi-Fi.

Tara Angkor Hotel, Siem Reap

 Tara Angkor Hotel is the 4-Star Luxury Hotel built in the mystical land of Angkor. Ideally and conveniently located. Tara Angkor Hotel is situated only 6 km from the World Heritage site of Angkor Wat Temples, 15 min drive from the Siem Reap International Airport, a few minutes stroll to the Angkor National Museum and a short ride to the city town center with an array of Cambodian souvenirs, shopping and culture.

Guests can approach the 24-hour front desk for currency exchange, tour arrangements, ticketing and concierge services. Alternatively, guests can exercise in the fitness centre or relax in the sauna. T

accommodations.description:
Harmony Phnom Penh Hotel

 Harmony Phnom Penh Hotel is within a 5-minute walk from the Royal Palace. The property is just 500 metres from the Riverfront Park, while Wat Phnom and Chaktomouk Conference Hall 2 are 1 km away. It is 3.8 km to Aeon Mall. Phnom Penh International Airport is 9 km from Harmony Phnom Penh Hotel.
Fitted with parquet flooring, air-conditioned rooms open up to views of the city. The seating area is fitted with a flat-screen TV, minibar and a desk. En suite bathrooms include shower facilities, a hairdryer and free toiletries.
Guests can approach the 24-hour front desk for currency exchange, business facilities and concierge services. A fitness centre is available for working out or guests can indulge in in-house spa treatments. Guests may also rent a car to explore the

accommodations.name: Emm Hotel Saigon
accommodations.description:
Emm Hotel Saigon

 Centrally located between Saigon’s glittery downtown of District 1 and its historic homes of District 3, ÊMM Hotel Saigon is an easy walk to such city icons as Notre Dame Cathedral and Unification Palace as well as a variety of restaurants, shopping centers and local markets. For guests traveling by air, ÊMM Hotel Saigon is just a 15-minute taxi ride from Tan Son Nhat International Airport.

accommodations.name: La Regina Royal Cruise, Halong
accommodations.description:
La Regina Royal Cruise, Halong

 Known as the charming younger sister of La Regina Legend, La
Regina Royal is not merely as elegant and luxurious in every detail as her
sister, but also youth oriented with a cozy atmosphere and a delightful blend
of traditional Vietnamese design. A cruise trip with La Regina Royal is a
combination of the bay’s most magnificent scenery, local attractions and on
board amenities. Get ready for your most unforgettable moment on La Regina
Royal.

accommodations.name: Grand Citidel Hotel, Hanoi
accommodations.description:
Grand Citidel Hotel, Hanoi

 Hanoi is a charming and enchanting city. Grand Cititel Hanoi is where culture and art merge in the vibrant heart of Hanoi, offering customers an authentic experience, immersing them in the world of exquisite art and understated yet distinctive elegance. Our hotel boasts 97 rooms, a restaurant, a gym, a welcoming lobby, a stylish bar, and a stress-relieving spa, providing a haven for relaxation and comfort. With three luxurious room categories and naturally illuminated event spaces, our hotel offers a space that is sophisticated, practical, and more inviting than ever.

accommodations.name: Hoi An Beach Resort
accommodations.description:
Hoi An Beach Resort

 Nestled between Cua Dai Beach and De Vong River, Hoi An Beach Resort features 2 outdoor pools. Hoi An Beach Resort is a 45-minute drive from Danang International Airport and 4 km from Hoi An’s town centre. Rooms at Resort Hoi An come with private balconies overlooking the garden, river or sea. Each room is equipped with a TV, safety deposit box and tea/coffee making facilities. Local cooking classes begin with a guided boat trip to Hoi An Market. Waterlily Spa offers Vietnamese massage therapies. Other recreational activities include a game of billiards or a workout in the fitness centre. At River Breeze Restaurant, guests can eat indoors or on the balcony overlooking the river. Snacks and refreshments can be enjoyed at the Sunshine Bar and the beachfront Sands Bar.

title: 14 Nights Cambodia Vietnam and Singapore
description:
With a picture-perfect setting on the Indochina Peninsula, Vietnam, Cambodia and Singapore are exquisite destinations. Boasting crumbling ancient temples, beautiful lakes, cosmopolitan cities and some of the most mind-blowing scenery on the planet, it’s no wonder Southeast Asia has skyrocketed to the top of travel-to-do lists worldwide.

Your voyage will begin with 11 nights touring Cambodia and Vietnam.  You will have the opportunity to venture into the jungle’s creepers towards Angkor Wat, the 12th century temple and shrine of Khmer art and architecture, a Cambodian mascot with its sculpted towers of lotus blossom.

Next, wander through the ancient capital of Khmer, empire to the cities of Siem Reap, Ho Chi Minh and Hanoi, before cruising in Agatha Christie style across Halong Bay, passing some of the 3,000 limestone islands. Add spice by devouring the Vietnamese cuisine of Ben Thành Market infused with a vast spectrum of enticing and evocative flavours, making taste buds explode!

You’ll end your adventure, with 3 exciting nights exploring the island city-state of Singapore. Why not spend a day visiting some of Asia’s best museums, an afternoon at Sri Mariammam Temple or take a trip on the Singapore Flyer – a huge Ferris wheel that offers panoramic views over the city.

Good to know: This 14-night offer includes stays at multi top-rated hotels and cruise connections. Breakfast is included at the hotels. We’ve also included transfers and return flights from the UK.

Solo Travellers can also explore the wonders of this tour alongside like-minded travellers, and with the peace of mind of travelling within a group - Select dates from 1799 !

Spotless and orderly, the island city state of Singapore has a flawless reputation which makes it a special delight for travelers to discover on their holiday to Southeast Asia. With English spoken by most the locals and an easy to navigate transport system, Singapore is known as the most accessible of Asia’s great cities. Most of all, Singapore is bursting with a culturally rich- multi-ethnic mix of Chinese, Malay, Indian and other influences, all of whom maintain a sense of tradition against the evolving backdrop of modern Singapore. 

OVERNIGHT IN SINGAPORE

itinerary.title: SINGAPORE-SENTOSA ISLAND
itinerary.description:
After Breakfast, it's an Exciting day ahead until the Sunset. In the afternoon you will be picked up from the hotel for an exciting Afternoon till Sunset excursion. Soar high above Singapore as you travel to the island resort of Sentosa via the Singapore Cable Car’s Mount Faber line. Enjoy scenic views of the city and cross the harbour before landing on Sentosa. Upon arrival, head to the top of the Merlion Tower, a perfect spot to take photos of the iconic Merlion. Visit Sentosa 4D AdventureLand and enjoy an once-in-a-lifetime adventure in Journey 2: The Mysterious Island The 4-D Experience. Join Sean and his friends in their search for the lost city of Atlantis in this immersive 4D experience. 

Next, you will go on a unique and fun journey through history at Images of Singapore LIVE, an interactive experience which tells Singapore’s exceptional story through a combination of live actors and special effects. 

Then get up close to famous Asian and international stars from the music, sports and Hollywood film industry at Madame Tussauds Singapore wax museum. Pose for the paparazzi or take selfies with icons like Brad Pitt, Yao Ming or Bruce Lee. 

End the day with the sound, laser, water and fireworks spectacular show Wings of Time at Siloso Beach where you can enjoy priority entry and premium seats with the best views of the fountains and pyrotechnics lighting up the sky against an open sea backdrop.

Return to the hotel. 

OVERNIGHT IN SINGAPORE

itinerary.title: SINGAPORE

title: 10 Nights Single Traveler Cambodia and Vietnam Trip
description:
During this fantastic trip, undergo an exhilarating renovation of the senses. Venture into the jungle’s vines and creepers towards Angkor Wat, the 12th century temple and shrine of Khmer art and architecture, a Cambodian mascot with its sculpted towers of lotus blossom and stately surroundings worshiped by Buddhists monks.

Next up is Vietnam with are breathtaking destinations of diverse delights. Travelers are gripped by the sights and sounds, bewitched by their geniality and divine cuisine, captivated by fast-moving cities like Ho Chi Minh, the Mecca in which Vietnam flourishes, and enlightened by the palaces, cathedrals and the thousands of stalagmites of Sung Sot cave.

Such a concoction of history, French colonial influences, and tales of past upheaval ensures a majestic holiday. This trip also includes Cruise in the Halong Bay, a UNESCO world heritage Site. Lunch on Board with a Free Bottle of Wine, with a lot of Sights & activities along the way.

itinerary.title: ARRIVE SIEM REAP--DAY AT LEISURE
itinerary.description:
You will be received with a warm welcome at Siem Reap International airport and transferred to the hotel. The evening is free for you to relax at the hotel. In case you wish to explore the city, you can choose to visit Pub Street which is famous for its quality yet economical restaurants and bars. Enjoy Khmer dinner on the day of arrival.

OVERNIGHT IN SIEM REAP

itinerary.title: FULL DAY ANGKOR TOUR
itinerary.description:
After a sumptuous breakfast at the hotel, you’ll enjoy a full-day tour of the Angkor complex. You must not miss the antique capital of Angkor Thom. With sites like the South Gate with its huge statues depicting the churning of the ocean of milk; the Bayon Temple, unique for its 54 towers decorated with over 200 smiling faces of Avolokitesvara; the Phimeanakas; the Royal Enclosure; the Elephants Terrace and the Terrace of the Leper King; Angkor Thom has so much to offer. 

The most famous of all the temples on the plain of Angkor is Angkor Wats. The temple complex covers 81 hectares and is comparable in size to the Imperial Palace in Beijing. Its distinctive five towers are emblazoned on the Cambodian flag and the 12th century masterpiece is considered by art historians to be the prime example of classical Khmer art and architecture. Other sites that deserve a mention are: Prasat Kravan, also known as ‘The Royal Baths’, the site was once used for ritual bathing; Banteay Kdei, surrounded by 4 concentric walls; Neak Pean, a fountain built in the middle of a pool; Preah Khan temple, built by the King Jayavarman VII.

OVERNIGHT IN SIEM REAP

itinerary.title: SIEM REAP - --DAY AT LEISURE OR OPTIONAL BOAT TRIP
itinerary.description:
After eating breakfast at the hotel, your day will be at leisure or you may head out to enjoy an optional boat ride on the Tonle Sap Lake. This beautiful fresh-water lake is the largest in South-east Asia and flows into Tonle Sap River, joining the Mekong in Phnom Penh. Built on the lake, is a wondrous ‘floating village’ with floating schools, floating police station, et al. The ‘village’ moves from place to place following water levels and current.

OVERNIGHT IN SIEM REAP

itinerary.title: SIEM REAP - PHNOM PENH
itinerary.description:
After breakfast get ready for a coach journey from Siem Reap to Phnom Penh. On arrival, you will meet one of our representative and transferred to your hotel in Phnom Penh.

Continue your journey in the Pearl of the Orient, Phnom Penh, visiting by yourself the dazzling white and gold complex of the Royal Palace and the Silver Pagoda. Feel free to visit the Genocide Museum or venture to the former Tuol Svay Prey High School, which the Khmer Rouge set up as prison in May 1976, to detain those accused of opposing the Pol Pot regime. Be prepared to be shaken by this moving reminder of the genocide that occurred during Cambodia’s Khmer Rouge regime.

OVERNIGHT IN PHNOM PENH

itinerary.title: PHNOM PENH - HO CHI MINH CITY
itinerary.description:
After breakfast at the hotel, we depart to Ho Chi Minh City by morning bus (Giant Ibis). Upon arrival at Ho Chi Minh City, you are transferred to the hotel. If there’s time, you must stroll around the downtown part of the bustling Ho Chi Minh City to explore the different local ways of life. Ho Chi Minh City, still called Saigon by many locals, is a centre of commerce, finance, culture and tourism in Vietnam. As opposed to its northern counterpart, this metropolis is filled with automobiles, numerous shopping areas and sidewalk cafes.

OVERNIGHT IN HO CHI MINH CITY

itinerary.title: HO CHI MINH CITY SIGHTS & CU CHI TUNNELS EXCURSION
itinerary.description:
The plan is to devote half of today to exploring captivating Ho Chi Minh City. We pass by the now-demolished wartime American Embassy on our way to the Reunification Palace. This famous edifice was a former residence of the President of Southern Vietnam until end of April 1975. We also visit some striking French colonial structures including the Notre Dame Cathedral and the Old Saigon Post Office. Post this, we head to the Jade Emperor Pagoda and the War Remnant Museum. We conclude our sightseeing session with a walk around the retail Ben Thanh Market where anything and everything is for sale! In the afternoon, we travel about 30 km North-West of Ho Chi Minh City to Cu Chi town. 

Cu Chi tunnels were used as the base from which the Vietnamese mounted their operations of the Tet Offensive in 1968. The incredible underground network in Cu Chi stretched over 200 kilometres and became legendary during the American war. The extensive tunnels have been specially constructed with living areas, weapon factories, filed hospitals, command centres, plus accommodation. We visit an exposition hall and a widened section of the tunnels to get a feel of the underground life. There are also possibilities to fire off rounds from an AK47 or MK16 at the nearby rifle range.

OVERNIGHT IN HO CHI MINH CITY

itinerary.title: SAIGON - HANOI--EVENING AT LEISURE
itinerary.description:
Step back in time as you fly from the buzzing, modern city of Ho Chi Minh to Hanoi. Upon arrival at Noibai Hanoi Airport, you’ll be met by our tour guide & transferred to your hotel in Hanoi. Afternoon / Evening at leisure to explore the evening sights on your own.

OVERNIGHT IN HANOI

itinerary.title: HANOI - HALONG PIER - CRUISE
itinerary.description:
An Early morning start today to get you to the Halong Pier, you will be picked up from your hotel with a packed breakfast. We arrive at Halong tourist wharf. Halong Bay has been recognized by UNESCO as a World Heritage Site since 1994. The islands in Halong Bay are mainly limestone and schist islands. Karst, the result of repeated rising and lowering of the continent, underwent full erosion and weathering to create the unique Halong Bay in the world. 

We travel to Cruise where you are welcomed by a fresh drink, cruise briefing & safety instructions before setting you free on the deck to explore this Natural wonder. After Sightseeing you will be served with a Vietnamese sea-food lunch & Wine, while cruising towards Surprising Cave. In the evening you will disembark the Cruise for your road trip back to Hanoi. Evening is at leisure to stroll past the Hoan Kiem Lake or enjoy drink and dinner at one of the specialized Singles Pub.

OVERNIGHT IN HANOI

itinerary.title: HANOI
itinerary.description:
After breakfast at the hotel, you will enjoy a walking tour of the Ho Chi Minh complex, the Ho Chi Minh’s Mausoleum - the final resting place of Vietnamese great father; President Ho Chi Minh’s stilt house - where Ho lived on and off from 1958 to 1969. The next place is One Pillar Pagoda, a group of structures consisting of a pagoda and a tower built in the middle of a square pond. From there, leave for the Temple of Literature, the first college of Vietnam. While heading back to Hoan Kiem Lake, have a brief stopover at Ngoc Son Temple. Thereafter, you can take a Cyclo tour around the Old Quarter Streets.

OVERNIGHT IN HANOI

itinerary.title: HANOI--DAY AT LEISURE
itinerary.description:
Have a leisurely breakfast at the hotel. The day is at leisure to walk around the lake. You can choose to visit the Church, the famous red bridge. In the evening, you will enjoy the Water Puppet Show near the lake (Tickets will be provided).

OVERNIGHT IN HANOI

title: Laos, Cambodia and Vietnam Holiday
description:
We’re offering you the chance to spend a fortnight discovering three of Asia’s most exquisite countries: Laos, Cambodia and Vietnam. Pack your bags and get ready for a heavy dose of history and heritage as you explore the likes of Ha Long Bay, Phnom Penh and Ho Chi Minh City. 

Your first stop on this roller coaster ride through Southeast Asia is Laos. Though a country once eclipsed by other Southeast Asian heavyweights such as Thailand and Vietnam, Laos has really come into its own within recent years, adopting the tourism slogan “Laos, Simply Beautiful” and a laid-back lifestyle characterised by glorious sunsets spilling over into the Mekong River and prime status as the “least Westernised” of all its neighbours. Picture breath-taking wilderness, untouched local villages and marvellous river views where Mekong pink dolphins scurry beneath the surf. When you’re not exploring the famous Tam Ting Cave with its golden Buddha statues, you’ll be rubbing shoulders with the locals in the tribal village of Ban Xom or dipping your toes in the glorious Khouang Si Waterfalls before heading to your next destination, Cambodia, a temple-ridden paradise of verdant mountain ranges and dreamy beaches. 

Although Cambodia’s history has been anything but peaceful, the beauty running through the core of this country is undeniably stunning. Home to the Cardamom Mountains and the golden beaches of Koh Kong, Cambodia offers something for everyone. Probably one of the most striking parts of your trip will be the fantastic tour of Angkor, the former capital city of the Khmer Empire which houses the majestic Angkor Wat Temple complex, impossibly beautiful and serene. You’ll also have the chance to meander through the Cambodian capital of Phnom Penh, a city which sits along the rippling banks of the Tonle Sap and Mekong River, leafy and idyllic, and visit the Cambodian Buddhist Wats too. 

Next, say good morning to Vietnam! Ho Chi Minh, formerly Saigon, will give you your first taste of Vietnamese culture. Dotted around the city you’ll stumble across French colonial landmarks and Vietnam War history museums, reminiscent of the country’s turbulent past. Prepare for a tour around the underground Cu Chi tunnels which served as hideouts and communication routes for the Viet Cong. Then, swap the hustle of bustle of Ho Chi Minh for the “east-meets-west” charm of the city of Hanoi, Vietnam’s capital, where sumptuous cuisine and glistening temples reign. To the east of Hanoi, you’ll find the incredible Halong Bay, often considered one of the natural wonders of the world. An overnight stay on a Flamingo Cruise will provide ample opportunity for sunset viewing and beach and cove exploration, in addition to a sun-deck cooking class guaranteed to turn you into the Gordon Ramsay of Vietnamese food.
